item.title: Here’s what happens when you start AI policy with values, not tools
item.description: At Royal Holloway, the creation of an AI policy became a moment of profound reflection on institutional ethics and purpose. Lucy Gill-Simmen and Will Will Shüler elaborate

item.title: Safeguarding the art of lecturing in an AI age
item.description: Students are using AI as a personal tutor, but AI is using materials prepared by academics in order to do this. Shonagh Douglas and Lisa Collie ask who is looking after the interests of academics here?

item.title: Learning community means even more in the age of AI
item.description: Debbie McVitty posits that human interaction matters in learning not because it's "better" but simply because it's human

item.title: Educating for humans in the lead
item.description: Mark Peace posits that our anxiety about the threats of AI to standards risk blinding us to a deeper need to reassert the value of humanness in knowledge work

item.title: The Office of the Independent Adjudicator is reviewing its Scheme rules, and it wants you involved
item.description: With student complaints at record highs and the higher education landscape changing fast, Independent Adjudicator Helen Megarry explains why the time is right for a comprehensive review of the OIA’s Scheme

item.title: What the first National Disabled Staff Survey tells us
item.description: The first National Disabled Staff Survey exposes the deep structural barriers faced by disabled staff in higher education. Susan Wilbraham, Ruth Gilligan, and Jackie Carter draw on the voices of the sector to explain more

item.title: Four years on, research excellence in wartime is not a luxury – it is infrastructure
item.description: Anzhela Stashchak shows how the experience of UK-Ukraine research collaboration demonstrates the critical importance of structures when systems and individuals are under pressure

item.title: The support paradox is a poverty problem
item.description: Life satisfaction is up, but money worries, isolation and pre-existing need exacerbate underlying problems. Jim Dickinson wonders if we're reaching the limits of what universities can do on mental health

item.title: Pronouns, phronesis, and the perils of polite bureaucracy
item.description: Sunny Dhillon argues that strategic essentialism around gender risks undermining the intersectional approach universities claim to champion

item.title: Wires within wires – the hidden complexity of managing higher education assessment
item.description: Debbie McVitty finds out why the people who administer university assessment are navigating an ever more tangled landscape – and why that complexity is not a sign of failure
